proposed_comments.title: Read the Robocopy UI module settings file

confidence.rationale: SaveOptionsButton_Click reads RobocopyUISettings without the module identifier; the current pinned source still uses the default overload.

proposed_comments.body:
### Read the Robocopy UI module settings file

**Severity:** `high`

`GetSettings<RobocopyUISettings>()` uses the default settings overload, whose module name defaults to an empty string. The `UseLegacySaveMode` setting belongs to the Robocopy UI module, so this reads the root settings file instead and can ignore the value configured for `.rcj` saves. Pass `RobocopyUISettings.ModuleName` to the module-aware settings accessor.

```suggestion
        if (SettingsUtils.Default.GetSettingsOrDefault<RobocopyUISettings>(RobocopyUISettings.ModuleName).Properties.UseLegacySaveMode.Value)
```

proposed_comments.title: Gate the launch waiter on the module lifecycle

confidence.rationale: The constructor starts the global event waiter unconditionally; disable does not stop it, and process state has no synchronization.

proposed_comments.body:
### Gate the launch waiter on the module lifecycle

**Severity:** `high`

The constructor starts the named-event waiter while `_enabled` is false. `disable()` only clears that flag, and the callback calls `StartProcess()` without an enabled-state check. Consequently, a launch-event signal after an ordinary module disable still reaches `ShellExecuteExW`. The application's GPO check does not enforce the ordinary enable toggle. Also, `EventWaiter` invokes this callback on `WAIT_FAILED`, but the callback ignores its error argument and launches anyway.

Start the waiter in `enable()`, stop it in `disable()`, and return from the callback on unsuccessful wait results. Synchronize the tracked process state between the waiter thread and `call_custom_action()`; both currently check and update `m_process` without a lock. Single-instance registration in the application does not synchronize that native handle. Preserve deliberately supported custom-action launches separately.
